data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with strictly more total internal redundancy is more resilient because it can afford defense-in-depth and internally enforced architectural diversity, while decentralized operators converge on the same best practices under competitive pressure, eroding the diversity that would protect them.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Decentralized operators maintain diversity through regulatory mandates or protocol design","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service's internal diversity is undermined by internal homogenization pressures","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cost of enforced diversity exceeds the expected benefit of reduced correlated failure","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independent operators face competitive pressure to adopt best practices, leading to convergence on identical software stacks, cloud providers, and operational procedures. This convergence creates a correlated failure mode: all operators fail together when the shared best practice fails. A large service can enforce architectural diversity (multiple runtimes, redundant protocols, heterogeneous failure modes) that competitive independent operators cannot sustain because adopting a different practice is individually costly even if it is collectively beneficial. The large service's enforced diversity is a public good that the market cannot provide.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
